[#reference-files]
== Files and settings

Where `ws-host` keeps things, following the XDG conventions, and what your configuration may say.

[cols="2,4"]
|===
|Place |What is there

|`~/.config/workspaces-host/ws-host.env`
|your configuration

|`~/.config/workspaces-host/secrets.env`
|secrets, refused unless only you can read it (mode 600); `gh` and `glab` keep theirs in their own storage

|`~/.local/share/workspaces-host/tools/<name>/<version>`
|downloaded tools, with a `current` link to the installed version

|`~/.local/share/workspaces-host/enabled/<repo>`
|one link per repository you trust: the record of trust

|`~/.local/state/workspaces-host/`
|logs of what changed, and the commit each trust was given at

|`~/.cache/workspaces-host/`
|downloads, kept by fingerprint

|`~/.local/bin/ws-host`
|a link to the launcher in the workspaces-host clone

|`~/workspaces/<host>/<org>/<repo>`
|every repository

|`<repo>/.workspaces-host/ws-host.env`
|what a repository needs: its kit and the repositories it is worked beside

|===

=== Your configuration

[cols="2,5"]
|===
|Key |Meaning

|`WS_HOST_GIT_NAME`|the name to put on your commits
|`WS_HOST_GIT_EMAIL`|the email to put on your commits
|`WS_HOST_WORKSPACES`|the folder repositories are copied under (default ~/workspaces)
|`WS_HOST_GITLAB_HOSTS`|GitLab hosts you sign in to, space-separated
|`WS_HOST_REPOS`|the repositories you work in, as host/org/repo, space-separated (the two starter repositories when you say nothing)
|`WS_HOST_KIT`|kits to install for you whatever your repositories ask, space-separated (base and shell when you say nothing; empty for none)
|`WS_HOST_PROMPT`|the prompt setup gives bash and fish: pretty when you say nothing (needs a Nerd Font), plain (emoji and box lines only), or no to keep your own
|`WS_HOST_PROVIDERS`|whether VS Code setup asks to enable the repositories that declare themselves providers: yes when you say nothing, no to enable them yourself
|`WS_HOST_TRUSTED`|organizations whose repositories you trust, space-separated; only your own file can set this
|===

=== A repository's file

[cols="2,5"]
|===
|Key |Meaning

|`WS_HOST_KIT`|the kit the repository's tools need
|`WS_HOST_REPOS`|the repositories it is worked beside, as host/org/repo, space-separated
|`WS_HOST_VERSION`|the release of ws-host the repository is pinned to, where it pins one
|===

A file is `KEY=value` lines, the value optionally in quotes, `#` for a comment, a list on one line separated by spaces. Nothing is expanded and a line does not continue.
